name: Shangshan rice with domestication traits
description: Archaeological rice remains at Shangshan include plant-silica traits closer to domesticated than wild rice; researchers interpret them as evidence of an early domestication process.

impact.note: One site's rice remains showing early domestication traits; a new ability locally, on the line to Yangtze rice farming.

date.label: Approximately 9400 calibrated years BP (about 7450 BCE)
date.basis: Source-reported date or range. Calibrated BP converted using 1950 as reference year where indicated.

events.statement: Archaeological rice remains at Shangshan include plant-silica traits closer to domesticated than wild rice; researchers interpret them as evidence of an early domestication process.
events.caveats: The date is approximate and refers to sampled site material, not a dated invention or completed domestication. Wild, transitional and domestic interpretations are debated.

evidence.supports: Rice phytoliths at Shangshan are dated approximately 9400 cal BP; morphology suggests incipient domestication. Interpretation of domestication and precision of phytolith dating remain debated.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest evidence currently researched for this scoped record; not a claim of global priority. The date is approximate and refers to sampled site material, not a dated invention or completed domestication. Wild, transitional and domestic interpretations are debated.

caveats: The date is approximate and refers to sampled site material, not a dated invention or completed domestication. Wild, transitional and domestic interpretations are debated.

research.note: Independent check of the cited passages and marked facets on 2026-11-09; interpretations and date limits retain the stated caveats.

unresolved.note: Use-wear and rice husk residues on a Shangshan stone flake support panicle harvesting, while rachilla markings and soil phytoliths give independent evidence about rice morphology. Whether preferential harvesting and resowing contributed to the dated silica traits is unresolved.

evidence.locator: Integrating use-wear and phytolith results, Figs. 6–8; Discussion
evidence.supports: Supports rice panicle harvesting with stone flakes at Shangshan and offers a model for selection under repeated harvesting and seed retention.
Reports both wild-type and japonica-type rachilla markings in Shangshan material.
Dates phytoliths with traits interpreted as incipient domestication in a separate analysis.
